name: Biomedical Engineering
notes: 132 credit hours total: core 36, basic science & math 38, basic science electives 8, humanities/social sciences 16, PWR 4, professional writing 2, ULW 4, concentration 16, free electives 12.

Students choose one concentration: biomechanics, biosignals and biosystems, cell and tissue engineering, or medical optics (16 credits). Concentration course lists live in the BME Curriculum Guide PDF and are modeled here as a generic 16-credit BME 200+ group, flagged.

Basic science electives: two 110+ natural-science courses complementing the concentration; an approved/not-approved list exists (independent studies, BIOL 112/214/253, CHEM 137, some PHYS/EESC excluded) - not auto-enforced.
MATH 141/142/143 are equivalent to MATH 161/162; PHYS 121P/122P and PHYS 113 (with MATH 140 series) are accepted variants.
Cluster requirement is four humanities/social-science courses: a 3-course approved cluster (2.0 average) plus one more course.

requirementGroups.label: BME core courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: All of the following courses are required: BME 101/EAS 101; BME 201; BME 201P; BME 210; BME 221; BME 230; BME 245; BME 260; BME 295; BME 296

requirementGroups.label: Mathematics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Four math courses: MATH 161: Calculus IA*; MATH 162: Calculus IIA*; MATH 165: Linear Algebra with Differential Equations; MATH 164: Multidimensional Calculus (*MATH 141, 142, and 143 are equivalent to MATH 161 and 162)

requirementGroups.label: Chemistry
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Two chemistry courses: CHEM 131: CHM Concepts, Systems, Practice I; CHEM 132: CHM Concepts, Systems, Practice II

requirementGroups.label: Physics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Two physics courses: PHYS 121 or PHYS 121P: Mechanics or PHYS 113, if taking MATH 140 series; PHYS 122 or PHYS 122P: Electricity and Magnetism

requirementGroups.label: Biology
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One biology course: BIOL 110: Principles of Biology I

requirementGroups.label: Basic science electives (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: All students must complete at least two additional courses (at least eight credit hours) in the basic sciences ... Most natural science courses with a number of 110 or higher (biology, microbiology, environmental science, neuroscience, chemistry, physics, or selected courses from brain and cognitive sciences) may be used
requirementGroups.note: NEEDS nuance: department maintains approved/not-approved lists (only one cell-biology and one anatomy course count); no independent studies. Modeled as a filtered natural-science group.

requirementGroups.label: BME concentration (16 credits, one area)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students can then choose which area of biomedical engineering they want to specialize in by choosing one of the following concentration areas: Biomechanics; Biosignals and biosystems; Cell and tissue engineering; Medical optics. Biomedical engineering concentration courses: 16 credits.
requirementGroups.note: Each concentration is three named courses plus one upper-level BME (examples from the requirements page). Other upper-level BME courses and a custom concentration by petition may also count — confirm with the BME Curriculum Guide.

upperLevelWriting.label: Upper-level BME course (BME 221/230/260/296 or any upper-level BME)
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: The following courses, as well as any upper-level BME course, will satisfy this requirement including: BME 221; BME 230; BME 260; BME 296
upperLevelWriting.note: BME also requires a separate 2-credit professional writing requirement (WRTG 273) and the Primary Writing Requirement, counted separately in the 132-credit total.
